Default: Ollama. Pass use_claude=true to route to cowork.askClaude."`).
PART C — SA1–SA4 verbatim semantic anchors (load-bearing acceptance criteria, NOT mere field-renames). These four anchors must each land as a named Red test that fails BEFORE the corresponding UI feature lands, and as an explicit acceptance bullet in frontends-005's cycle 6.9 task list.
SA1 (still_indexing pill). Spec §11 verbatim: "Semantic-search code paths (`scholar.papers.search` with semantic mode) check `settings.chunk_vec.created` and degrade to lexical with a 'still indexing' pill when false — the same affordance used for partially-embedded chunks." (spec line 1007; identical phrasing reused at spec line 1346). Frontends MUST render a "still indexing" pill in `CorpusDashboard` and `PaperDetail` views when `searchResult.still_indexing === true`. Red test in `src/ui/views/CorpusDashboard.test.tsx`: pill present when mock has `still_indexing: true`; pill absent when `false`.
SA2 (askClaude sentinel + host-capability detection). Spec §11 verbatim: "On seeing `structuredContent.askClaude`, the UI calls `window.cowork.askClaude(askClaude.prompt, askClaude.data)` (a host-provided global in the MCP App iframe) and renders the result. This sentinel shape is the contract shared between the producers (`src/server/tools/digest.ts`, `prompts.ts`) and the consumer (`src/ui/views/DigestPanel.tsx`)." (spec lines 1015-1028, see also F8 host-capability prose at spec lines 1030-1035: "`window.cowork.askClaude` is a Cowork-host-provided global … The UI feature-detects with `typeof window.cowork?.askClaude === 'function'` on mount … Absent. The toggle is hidden entirely; in its place the UI renders a single static note: *'Claude fallback unavailable in this host.'* Servers still receive `askClaude: undefined` in tool calls (the toggle was never offered)"). Frontends `DigestPanel` + `ReadingPromptsPane` MUST (a) feature-detect `window.cowork?.askClaude` on mount, (b) hide the toggle entirely + render the static "Claude fallback unavailable in this host." note when absent, (c) forward `askClaude.prompt`/`askClaude.data` to `window.cowork.askClaude(...)` when the server returns `structuredContent.askClaude` and the host supports it. Two Red tests: capability-detect (host-absent path renders static note + omits toggle); sentinel-forwarding (host-present + structuredContent.askClaude present → window.cowork.askClaude called with prompt+data args).
SA3 (scope_key enum — digest scope contract). Spec §9.3 verbatim: "Defaults to the current scope. Shows the cached digest if recent; otherwise calls `app.callServerTool('digest.generate', {scope_key})` which runs the Ollama chat model against a `paperLine`-style corpus slice (preserving the Daisy prompt skeleton but rewriting it for Qwen)." (spec line 935). Spec §8.2 verbatim: `scope_key: text("scope_key").notNull()` (spec line 841). Frontends `DigestPanel` MUST construct tool args with `scope_key` (NOT `since`) and accept the four enum patterns: `"all" | "section:<label>" | "stale" | "selection:<hash>"`. Type-check Red test asserting tool-call args carry `scope_key` field matching one of the four enum patterns.
SA4 (use_claude opt-in — mechanical-LLM-default discipline). CLAUDE.md "Load-bearing invariants" verbatim: "Mechanical LLM → local Ollama. Embeddings, digest, and reading-prompts default to local Ollama. `cowork.askClaude` is an explicit per-request opt-in only — never the default path." Spec §11 verbatim: "Mechanical LLM work → **Ollama by default**; `cowork.askClaude` is opt-in only." (spec line 1361). Spec §1 risks-table verbatim: "Mechanical LLM work routes through local Ollama, not the Claude API." | "User directive." | "All routine syntheses, reading-prompt generation, and embedding production default to Ollama. `cowork.askClaude` is opt-in only for high-stakes synthesis." (spec line 66). Frontends MUST default `use_claude` to FALSE (or omit the field, which equals false at the server) on every `digest.generate` and `prompts.generate` tool call; the "use Claude instead" toggle (offered only when SA2's host-capability detect returns present) MUST set `use_claude: true` ONLY when explicitly toggled by the user. Two Red tests: default-tool-call shape has `use_claude: false` (or field omitted); toggle-on-then-fire test asserts `use_claude: true` rides the request.
PART D — Optional additives DEFERRED (lead disposition 2026-05-24): `snippet?: string` on `SearchHit` and `papers_referenced: string[]` on `GenerateResult` are NOT included in v1; defer to v1.1. Do NOT add these to frontends-005.

GAP 1 — Add happy-dom + Bun test preload for DOM-based SA1-SA4 verbatim Red tests. - Add `@happy-dom/global-registrator` as a devDependency in package.json. Pin to the latest stable (verify via `bun add --dev @happy-dom/global-registrator` then commit the resulting package.json + bun.lock). - Create `bunfig.toml` at repo root (if not already present) with `[test]` section containing `preload = ["./test-preload.ts"]`. If bunfig.toml exists, MERGE rather than overwrite — preserve any existing config. - Create `test-preload.ts` at repo root with the minimal preload script: ```typescript import { GlobalRegistrator } from "@happy-dom/global-registrator"; GlobalRegistrator.register(); ``` - Verify by running `bun test src/server/extraction/chunker.test.ts` (a known-passing pre-existing test) — should still pass. Then verify `typeof document !== "undefined"` inside a throwaway test — should now be true (where it was undefined before). - Pin rationale (record in commit message): Bun 1.3.11 does NOT support a `--dom` test flag; the plan-md assumption (Tasks 1.5, 5.5, 7.5, 8b) is incorrect. happy-dom is the canonical Bun-compatible DOM library, ~150KB devDep, no runtime cost. Preserves chore 1c9e0d3's SA1-SA4 verbatim Red-test contracts without weakening them.
GAP 2 — Thread ctx through registerUiResource at src/server/index.ts. - Inspect src/server/index.ts around line 160 to find `registerUiResource(server)`. The `ctx` variable is in scope at lines 145-155 (per frontends teammate's empirical check); the change is `registerUiResource(server)` → `registerUiResource(server, ctx)`. - Inspect src/server/ui/resource.ts (foundation-scaffolded stub per Task 1.10b — referenced by chore 9d78da3's verbatim anchors). Widen its signature to accept `ctx` as the second arg if it doesn't already. The stub should compile cleanly with the new arg even though it doesn't yet use it — frontends teammate fills the body at cycle 6.9. - Verify by running `bunx tsc --noEmit` — must compile clean. Run `bun test` — must still pass (231 currently, +0 expected since this is a signature widen with no behavior change).
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - Single work commit landing both gaps. - Commit message format: `feat(foundation-fill): happy-dom DOM-test preload + ctx thread to registerUiResource`. - Final commit message body lists both gap-fixes explicitly (so the audit trail names what landed). - `bun test` passes 231+ (no regressions). - `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Final stdout: `WORK_COMMIT_SHA=<the new commit's SHA>` (PLEASE include this; the prior two chore-executors omitted it and forced the orchestrator into git-log inspection).
WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE - Do NOT fill the body of src/server/ui/resource.ts beyond the signature widen — that's frontends teammate at cycle 6.9. - Do NOT add any other React/test deps (react-test-renderer, @testing-library/react, etc.) — happy-dom alone is sufficient for the SA1-SA4 tests as authored in chore 1c9e0d3. - Do NOT edit src/server/tools/*.ts, src/server/extraction/*, src/server/ingest/* (all closed wave-1/2/3 plans). - Do NOT touch .claude/context/chores.xml — orchestrator owns the status flip. - Do NOT touch plans.xml, splits.xml, sequence.xml. - Do NOT modify any spec file.

Isolate the @happy-dom/global-registrator preload to opt-in UI-test usage. The prior chore foundation-fill-frontends-prereqs-dom-and-ctx (closed at 5e129f5) registered DOM globals via `bunfig.toml [test] preload = ["./test-preload.ts"]` where test-preload.ts unconditionally calls GlobalRegistrator.register(). This globally pollutes ALL test files with happy-dom's DOM shims (window, document, fetch, Response, Request) — incompatible with Bun.serve-based test stubs in 4 pre-existing server tests: - src/server/tools/prompts.test.ts: 2 fails (Bun.serve stub Ollama → fetch returns happy-dom Response → JSON parse fails) - src/server/tools/digest.test.ts: 1 fail (same Bun.serve stub Ollama pattern) - src/server/ingest/arxiv.test.ts: 1 fail (real fetch path; PDF bytes expected 37 received 91 — happy-dom Response.body normalization differs)
FIX (per frontends teammate's recommendation, lead-concurred): 1. Remove the `[test] preload` line from bunfig.toml (or remove the bunfig.toml file entirely if the only content was the [test] section). 2. Rename test-preload.ts → test-dom-helpers.ts at repo root (or keep the same filename if you prefer; both work). Replace the unconditional GlobalRegistrator.register() call with two named exports: ```typescript import { GlobalRegistrator } from "@happy-dom/global-registrator";
export function registerDom(): void { GlobalRegistrator.register(); }
export function unregisterDom(): void { GlobalRegistrator.unregister(); } ``` 3. Verify no test file currently imports from test-preload.ts (the global preload was the only consumer). If frontends teammate authored anything that imports it, flag in commit message — but at commit time they have not yet authored cycle 6.9 UI tests.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: - bunfig.toml's [test] preload line removed (or file removed entirely). - test-dom-helpers.ts (or test-preload.ts, your choice) exports registerDom + unregisterDom. - `bun test` returns to 242 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail (231 pre-Gap-1 baseline + 11 new nu-module tests landed at 6bdc167 = 242). The 4 happy-dom-induced regressions are GONE. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Single work commit. Commit message format: ``` fix(foundation-fill): isolate happy-dom DOM-shims to opt-in registerDom helper
Replaces global GlobalRegistrator.register() preload (which polluted ALL test files with happy-dom Response/fetch overrides) with opt-in registerDom/unregisterDom helpers consumed via beforeAll/afterAll in UI tests only. Closes chore foundation-isolate-happy-dom-to-ui- tests-only. Restores prompts/digest/arxiv server-test gate.
Gate: bun test 242 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail; bunx tsc --noEmit clean.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com> ``` - Final stdout: `WORK_COMMIT_SHA=<the new commit's SHA>`. (PLEASE include this stdout marker.)

Fix the foundation-declared `bun run build:ui` script in package.json so it handles Bun's HTML-bundler multi-file output (HTML entrypoint + JS chunks + sourcemaps + assets) correctly. Frontends teammate worked around this at cycle 6.9 (e84621d) by inlining `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["src/ui/index.html"], outdir: "dist/ui", target: "browser", minify: true })` into scripts/measure-bundle.ts so the cycle-6.9 bundle artifact + size-budget test could land. The workaround is scope-conformant (frontends BR includes scripts/measure-bundle.ts because it's pre-declared in package.json scripts as `measure-bundle`) but leaves the public `build:ui` entrypoint broken. Packaging cycle 6.13 (the .plugin archive assembler) will need a working build:ui to bundle the UI assets into the redistributable. Fix options: (a) extract the Bun.build invocation from measure-bundle.ts into scripts/build-ui.ts, point `build:ui` at it, leave measure-bundle.ts importing the helper (DRY); (b) inline the same Bun.build invocation directly in package.json's `build:ui` script via `bun -e '...'` (no new file, less DRY but minimal); (c) drop the public build:ui script entirely and have packaging-006 cycle 6.13 inline the bundle invocation. Recommendation: (a) — produces a stable scripts/build-ui.ts entrypoint that packaging-006 can import + invoke. Tier: interpretive (sonnet) — judgment on the helper signature (dist dir argument? minify flag? sourcemap toggle?) + matching the existing measure-bundle.ts invocation byte-for-byte. Vehicle: spec-pipeline:chore-executor. Acceptance: (1) `bun run build:ui` emits HTML + JS chunks + sourcemaps to dist/ui/; (2) scripts/measure-bundle.ts continues to work (imports or duplicates the build invocation); (3) `bun test` still passes 266+; (4) tsc clean. BLOCKS packaging cycle 6.13 because the .plugin archive assembly path needs a working build:ui to embed UI assets.

Reconcile spec §14.1 step 4 / step 5 prose with foundation's actual package.json field semantics for scholar.bundledBunVersion and scholar.bunSqliteVersion. Spec wording (line ~1361 area): "scholar.bundledBunVersion ... must match scholar.bunSqliteVersion from step 5 (both are read from the same Bun release)" — interpretable as string-equality check. Packaging cycle 6.13 implemented assertVersionInvariant accordingly: aborts SCHOLAR_BUILD_MISMATCH on string-diff. But foundation populated the fields as: bundledBunVersion="1.3.11" (Bun runtime version, from `bun --version`) and bunSqliteVersion="3.51.2" (the SQLite library version Bun's bun:sqlite links — these are DIFFERENT semantic types, not the same string). Both legitimately "read from the same Bun release" but record different facts about it. A real production build would currently misfire on this string-inequality. Fix options: (a) Spec amendment: clarify §14.1 step 4 — fields record different facts about the same Bun release; the invariant check becomes "both fields populated + non-empty" rather than string-equality. Update scripts/build-plugin.ts:assertVersionInvariant to match. (b) Foundation alignment: collapse the two fields to a single canonical bundledBunVersion field, OR populate both fields with the same Bun release string (deferring the SQLite-version fact to a third field if needed). Recommendation: (a) preserves the existing field semantics (both are legitimately useful pieces of metadata) and is a smaller spec edit. Tier: interpretive (sonnet) — judgment on spec wording + matching assertVersionInvariant rewrite. Vehicle: spec-pipeline:chore-executor. Acceptance: (1) spec §14.1 step 4 prose clarifies field semantics; (2) scripts/build-plugin.ts:assertVersionInvariant updated to match the clarified invariant (e.g., check both fields populated + non-empty); (3) scripts/build-plugin.test.ts SCHOLAR_BUILD_MISMATCH test updated to match the new invariant (or replaced with a "missing/empty field" test); (4) `bun test` 275+ pass; (5) tsc clean. RELEASE-GATE chore (does not block plan-group close — same precedent as license-audit-vendored-pdf-server and foundation-fix-build-ui-script-for-multi-file-output); must resolve before first real .plugin production build.

Fill the three foundation-owned gaps that corpus plan-md references but foundation-007 did not ship, plus the §7.6 PdfChild contract extension for setRoots. Tier: interpretive (sonnet). Vehicle: spec-pipeline:chore-executor. Blocks all corpus cycles (6.3 + 6.11) and consequently every downstream wave; high-priority dispatch.
GAP 1 — allPdfRoots helper. Add to src/server/db/default-pdf-root.ts (alongside existing defaultPdfRoot), signature `allPdfRoots(tx: BunSQLiteDatabase, corpusId: string): string[]` per CLAUDE.md tx-first cross-plan helper convention. Returns all pdf_roots.path rows for corpusId in pdf_roots.created_at ascending order (used by corpus.activate's `ctx.pdf.setRoots(allPdfRoots(...))` and by scholar.roots.list). Empty array is valid (corpus exists, no roots configured — UI surfaces this as "configure a PDF root" affordance). Add unit test src/server/db/default-pdf-root.test.ts extension covering: empty result; single root; multiple roots in created_at order.
GAP 2 — writeRuntimeConfig helper. Create NEW file src/server/util/runtime-config.ts exporting: (a) interface `RuntimeConfig { activeCorpusId: string | null }` (extensible later); (b) `writeRuntimeConfig(data: RuntimeConfig, runtimeRoot: string): Promise<void>` performing atomic write to `${runtimeRoot}/config.json` via `tmp + fsync + rename` pattern (per plan-md line 25 "atomic tmp + fsync + rename"; use `Bun.file().writer()` or fs/promises with mkstemp + writeFile + fdatasync + rename); (c) `readRuntimeConfig(runtimeRoot: string): Promise<RuntimeConfig | null>` returning null when file absent. Atomicity invariant: a crash mid-write must NEVER leave config.json in a partial state — readers either see the prior value or the new one. Add tests src/server/util/runtime-config.test.ts covering: write-then-read roundtrip; null-when-missing; atomic-rename verified by checking absence of partial-write tmp file after success.
GAP 3 — real DB-backed buildConfigAccessor. Replace stub at src/server/index.ts:75-84 (the function whose self-comment reads "corpus plan (cycle 6.3) fills the real DB-backed implementation" — that delegation was an authoring mistake; ConfigAccessor is foundation-owned per §7.6, so foundation fills it here). The real implementation backs ConfigAccessor methods on the configDb: - `get<T>(key: string)`: SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key=?; JSON.parse the value; return undefined if no row. - `set(key: string, value: unknown)`: INSERT OR REPLACE INTO settings (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) with JSON.stringify(value). - `corpora()`: SELECT * FROM corpora ORDER BY created_at ASC; map to CorpusRow shape. - `activeCorpusId()`: SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key='activeCorpusId' (string or undefined). NOTE on activeCorpusId persistence: while corpus plan-md uses writeRuntimeConfig to persist activeCorpusId to runtime/config.json, ConfigAccessor.activeCorpusId() reads from the settings TABLE in the config DB. Corpus.activate is responsible for keeping both in sync (DB UPDATE is the durable point per plan-md M4; config.json is a denormalized cache for startup-time corpus restoration). Foundation does NOT have to coordinate the two surfaces — just provide the DB-backed read.
GAP 4 — §7.6 PdfChild contract extension. Extend src/server/tools/registry.ts PdfChild interface (lines 19-29) to add `setRoots(roots: string[]): Promise<void>`. Strict superset addition; the existing PdfChildHandle implementation in src/server/pdf/lifecycle.ts already exposes setRoots so no impl change needed there. Also update the test stub PdfChild factory in src/server/index.ts (lines 100-109 — the fallback when deps.spawnPdfChild is unset) to include `setRoots: async () => {}` so the type matches. Verify the production binding flow (productionSpawnPdfChild returns PdfChildHandle which satisfies the extended PdfChild) compiles clean — no cast needed at the binding site.

Post-S1 §13 v1.1 amendment introduced `ctx.pdfViews: Map<paper_id, viewUUID>` as the viewUUID resolution surface (refreshExtraction at src/server/tools/pdf.ts:141 calls `ctx.pdfViews.get(args.paper_id)`). The `fakeCtx` helper in src/server/tools/pdf.test.ts:63-92 was never updated to populate this map, so the 5 refresh-extraction tests fail at TypeError "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'ctx.pdfViews.get')". Production path is fine — real `scholar.pdf.open` populates the map — but the tests give zero green-suite assertion that refresh-extraction works end-to-end.
Fix: extend `fakeCtx` to accept an optional `pdfViews` arg (default `new Map()`), then have each test that calls refreshExtraction with paper_id "pN" pre-populate the map with a synthetic viewUUID. Cleanest pattern: synthesize viewUUID as `view-${paper_id}` and let each test do `fakeCtx(sqlite, { pdfViews: new Map([["p1", "view-p1"]]) })`. Tier: mechanical (haiku → sonnet depending on whether all 5 tests can use a shared helper). Acceptance: 5 refresh-extraction tests go green; the rest of the suite stays at 289 pass; typecheck clean. Single commit: `test(pdf): seed ctx.pdfViews fixture so refresh-extraction tests pass`.

`bun run build:ui` fails with `FileNotFound: failed to open root directory: src/ui` because package.json declares `bun --cwd=scripts build-ui`, which sets cwd to `scripts/` before invoking `bun build-ui` (resolves to `scripts/build-ui.ts`). The script then passes `"src/ui/index.html"` as entrypoint and `"build/ui"` as outdir — both relative to the cwd, so they resolve to `scripts/src/ui/index.html` and `scripts/build/ui` (neither exists). The same failure mode hits `bun run measure-bundle` (`bun --cwd=scripts measure-bundle`). Consequently `src/ui/bundle.test.ts` beforeAll silently swallows the build error, and the 3 bundle-budget tests fail on missing `build/ui/app.html` and `build/ui/bundle-budget.json`.
Fix options (pick A unless reason to keep --cwd=scripts): (A) Drop --cwd: change package.json to `"build:ui": "bun scripts/build-ui.ts"` and `"measure-bundle": "bun scripts/measure-bundle.ts"`. Both scripts already use repo-root-relative paths internally. (B) Anchor scripts to import.meta.dir: refactor build-ui.ts and measure-bundle.ts to resolve `src/ui/index.html` and `build/ui` via `path.join(import.meta.dir, "..", ...)` so cwd doesn't matter.
Acceptance: `bun run build:ui` succeeds and produces `build/ui/app.html`; `bun run measure-bundle` produces `build/ui/bundle-budget.json` matching the shape `bundle.test.ts` asserts (total_kb / threshold_kb / over_budget / per_dep[]); the 3 bundle.test.ts tests go green; full suite reaches 297 pass / 8 skip / 0 fail; typecheck clean. Tier: mechanical-with-interpretation (sonnet) — picking A vs B is a 30-second judgment, the edit itself is ≤5 LOC. Single commit: `fix(build): resolve build:ui + measure-bundle without --cwd=scripts`.
